caption.en: Before 1819: the monsoon winds carry ships between India, the Malay world and China, and every route through the Straits of Malacca passes the island at the tip of the peninsula.
caption.zh: 【待译】Before 1819: the monsoon winds carry ships between India, the Malay world and China, and every route through the Straits of Malacca passes the island at the tip of the peninsula.

caption.en: The fourteenth century: on the hill above the river mouth, now Fort Canning, archaeologists have found Chinese porcelain, glass and gold from a town that Chinese and Javanese writers called Danmaxi and Tumasik.
caption.zh: 【待译】The fourteenth century: on the hill above the river mouth, now Fort Canning, archaeologists have found Chinese porcelain, glass and gold from a town that Chinese and Javanese writers called Danmaxi and Tumasik.

caption.en: From the sixteenth century the island belongs to the Sultanate of Johor, whose rulers move between the Johor River and the Riau islands; Orang Laut sea people patrol the straits for them.
caption.zh: 【待译】From the sixteenth century the island belongs to the Sultanate of Johor, whose rulers move between the Johor River and the Riau islands; Orang Laut sea people patrol the straits for them.

caption.en: By 1818 the British hold Penang and the Dutch hold Malacca again; in Riau two sons of the late Sultan Mahmud are both claimed as his heir.
caption.zh: 【待译】By 1818 the British hold Penang and the Dutch hold Malacca again; in Riau two sons of the late Sultan Mahmud are both claimed as his heir.

caption.en: 28 January 1819: ships of the East India Company anchor off the Singapore River, where the Temenggong Abdul Rahman has his village.
caption.zh: 【待译】28 January 1819: ships of the East India Company anchor off the Singapore River, where the Temenggong Abdul Rahman has his village.

caption.en: Early February 1819: Hussein, elder son of the late Sultan Mahmud, is brought from the Riau islands; the British will recognise him as Sultan of Johor.
caption.zh: 【待译】Early February 1819: Hussein, elder son of the late Sultan Mahmud, is brought from the Riau islands; the British will recognise him as Sultan of Johor.

caption.en: 6 February 1819: Raffles, Sultan Hussein and the Temenggong sign a treaty allowing the Company to build a trading post here, in return for yearly payments.
caption.zh: 【待译】6 February 1819: Raffles, Sultan Hussein and the Temenggong sign a treaty allowing the Company to build a trading post here, in return for yearly payments.

caption.en: 1819: the Dutch in Malacca and Batavia protest that Singapore belongs to the Sultan they recognise in Riau; in Singapore, Farquhar is left in charge with a few hundred troops.
caption.zh: 【待译】1819: the Dutch in Malacca and Batavia protest that Singapore belongs to the Sultan they recognise in Riau; in Singapore, Farquhar is left in charge with a few hundred troops.

caption.en: November 1822: Raffles sets up a Town Committee; Lieutenant Jackson's plan divides the land around the river among the government, Europeans and each Asian community.
caption.zh: 【待译】November 1822: Raffles sets up a Town Committee; Lieutenant Jackson's plan divides the land around the river among the government, Europeans and each Asian community.

caption.en: 1822 to 1823: a small hill is cut down and its earth fills the swamp on the south bank; the shoreline you see here is the one after that first land reclamation.
caption.zh: 【待译】1822 to 1823: a small hill is cut down and its earth fills the swamp on the south bank; the shoreline you see here is the one after that first land reclamation.

caption.en: June 1823: the Sultan and the Temenggong give up most of their rights in the settlement for monthly allowances, and the Temenggong moves to Telok Blangah.
caption.zh: 【待译】June 1823: the Sultan and the Temenggong give up most of their rights in the settlement for monthly allowances, and the Temenggong moves to Telok Blangah.

caption.en: 1824: in London, Britain and the Netherlands divide the Malay world along the Straits; in August the Sultan and the Temenggong cede Singapore island to the Company for good.
caption.zh: 【待译】1824: in London, Britain and the Netherlands divide the Malay world along the Straits; in August the Sultan and the Temenggong cede Singapore island to the Company for good.

caption.en: 1826: Penang, Malacca and Singapore become one colony, the Straits Settlements, run by the East India Company from Calcutta.
caption.zh: 【待译】1826: Penang, Malacca and Singapore become one colony, the Straits Settlements, run by the East India Company from Calcutta.

caption.en: Around 1830: junks come south from Amoy and Canton on the north-east monsoon, Bugis traders sail in from Makassar, and country ships bring opium and cloth from India.
caption.zh: 【待译】Around 1830: junks come south from Amoy and Canton on the north-east monsoon, Bugis traders sail in from Makassar, and country ships bring opium and cloth from India.

caption.en: 1864: the Tanjong Pagar Dock Company opens wharves in deep water west of the town, ready for steamships.
caption.zh: 【待译】1864: the Tanjong Pagar Dock Company opens wharves in deep water west of the town, ready for steamships.

caption.en: 1867: the Straits Settlements become a Crown Colony; in 1869 the Suez Canal opens and steamships reach Singapore from Europe in weeks, not months.
caption.zh: 【待译】1867: the Straits Settlements become a Crown Colony; in 1869 the Suez Canal opens and steamships reach Singapore from Europe in weeks, not months.

caption.en: February 1821: the first junk from Amoy arrives in Singapore; over the next century millions of people from southern China will pass through this port.
caption.zh: 【待译】February 1821: the first junk from Amoy arrives in Singapore; over the next century millions of people from southern China will pass through this port.

caption.en: From 1825: convicts from India and from Bencoolen are shipped to Singapore; they build roads, bridges and public buildings.
caption.zh: 【待译】From 1825: convicts from India and from Bencoolen are shipped to Singapore; they build roads, bridges and public buildings.

caption.en: Mid-nineteenth century: Tamil and Chulia traders sail from the Coromandel coast, and Arab merchant families from Hadhramaut in southern Arabia settle in Singapore.
caption.zh: 【待译】Mid-nineteenth century: Tamil and Chulia traders sail from the Coromandel coast, and Arab merchant families from Hadhramaut in southern Arabia settle in Singapore.

caption.en: From across the archipelago come Bugis from Sulawesi, Javanese and Boyanese from Bawean island, many staying for good.
caption.zh: 【待译】From across the archipelago come Bugis from Sulawesi, Javanese and Boyanese from Bawean island, many staying for good.

caption.en: 1877: after years of complaints about kidnapping and cheating in the labour trade, the government opens a Chinese Protectorate under William Pickering.
caption.zh: 【待译】1877: after years of complaints about kidnapping and cheating in the labour trade, the government opens a Chinese Protectorate under William Pickering.

caption.en: 1827: on South Bridge Road, a Hindu temple and a Chulia mosque stand a short walk apart.
caption.zh: 【待译】1827: on South Bridge Road, a Hindu temple and a Chulia mosque stand a short walk apart.

caption.en: 1839 to 1844: Hokkien merchants build the Thian Hock Keng temple on Telok Ayer Street, then on the shore, and Tan Tock Seng pays for a hospital for the poor.
caption.zh: 【待译】1839 to 1844: Hokkien merchants build the Thian Hock Keng temple on Telok Ayer Street, then on the shore, and Tan Tock Seng pays for a hospital for the poor.

caption.en: May 1854: fighting between Hokkien and Teochew groups spreads from the town to the plantations and lasts about ten days; hundreds are killed.
caption.zh: 【待译】May 1854: fighting between Hokkien and Teochew groups spreads from the town to the plantations and lasts about ten days; hundreds are killed.

caption.en: 1879 to 1887: the bay in front of Telok Ayer Street is filled in; Robinson Road now runs where boats once anchored.
caption.zh: 【待译】1879 to 1887: the bay in front of Telok Ayer Street is filled in; Robinson Road now runs where boats once anchored.

caption.en: January 1874: at Pangkor, a disputed succession in Perak ends with a treaty that places a British Resident beside the Sultan.
caption.zh: 【待译】January 1874: at Pangkor, a disputed succession in Perak ends with a treaty that places a British Resident beside the Sultan.

caption.en: 1 July 1896: Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang are joined as the Federated Malay States, each keeping its Sultan.
caption.zh: 【待译】1 July 1896: Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang are joined as the Federated Malay States, each keeping its Sultan.

caption.en: 1909: Siam transfers Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu to British protection; with Johor they become the Unfederated Malay States.
caption.zh: 【待译】1909: Siam transfers Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu to British protection; with Johor they become the Unfederated Malay States.

caption.en: 15 February 1915: part of the 5th Light Infantry, an Indian regiment, mutinies; British, Asian and volunteer forces crush it within days, and dozens of mutineers are executed in public.
caption.zh: 【待译】15 February 1915: part of the 5th Light Infantry, an Indian regiment, mutinies; British, Asian and volunteer forces crush it within days, and dozens of mutineers are executed in public.

caption.en: 28 June 1924: the Causeway opens across the Johor Strait, carrying a railway and a road to the peninsula.
caption.zh: 【待译】28 June 1924: the Causeway opens across the Johor Strait, carrying a railway and a road to the peninsula.

caption.en: 8 December 1941: Japanese troops land at Kota Bharu, and more come ashore at Singora and Patani in southern Thailand.
caption.zh: 【待译】8 December 1941: Japanese troops land at Kota Bharu, and more come ashore at Singora and Patani in southern Thailand.

caption.en: February 1942: after a week of fighting on the island, including the Malay Regiment's stand at Bukit Chandu, the garrison of about 85,000 surrenders on 15 February.
caption.zh: 【待译】February 1942: after a week of fighting on the island, including the Malay Regiment's stand at Bukit Chandu, the garrison of about 85,000 surrenders on 15 February.

caption.en: At Changi Beach 66 men are killed on 20 February, and on Punggol beach some 400 on 28 February. Nobody counted the dead: the Japanese figure at the 1947 trial was about 5,000, Singapore's Chinese community puts it at up to 100,000, and most estimates lie between 25,000 and 50,000.
caption.zh: 【待译】At Changi Beach 66 men are killed on 20 February, and on Punggol beach some 400 on 28 February. Nobody counted the dead: the Japanese figure at the 1947 trial was about 5,000, Singapore's Chinese community puts it at up to 100,000, and most estimates lie between 25,000 and 50,000.

caption.en: October 1943: Japan hands Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu to its ally Thailand; in Singapore, food is rationed and the occupation money loses its value.
caption.zh: 【待译】October 1943: Japan hands Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu to its ally Thailand; in Singapore, food is rationed and the occupation money loses its value.

caption.en: 12 September 1945: in Singapore's Municipal Building, Admiral Mountbatten accepts the surrender of the Japanese forces in Southeast Asia.
caption.zh: 【待译】12 September 1945: in Singapore's Municipal Building, Admiral Mountbatten accepts the surrender of the Japanese forces in Southeast Asia.

caption.en: September 1945: the British return and set up a military administration; food is short, prices are high and the black market thrives.
caption.zh: 【待译】September 1945: the British return and set up a military administration; food is short, prices are high and the black market thrives.

caption.en: 1 April 1946: Singapore becomes a separate Crown Colony, while the peninsula's states and Penang and Malacca form the Malayan Union.
caption.zh: 【待译】1 April 1946: Singapore becomes a separate Crown Colony, while the peninsula's states and Penang and Malacca form the Malayan Union.

caption.en: June 1948: after the killing of planters in Perak, a state of Emergency is declared against the Malayan Communist Party's armed revolt; it will last twelve years.
caption.zh: 【待译】June 1948: after the killing of planters in Perak, a state of Emergency is declared against the Malayan Communist Party's armed revolt; it will last twelve years.

caption.en: 11 December 1950: a court ruling on the custody of Maria Hertogh sets off three days of rioting; 18 people are killed and 173 injured.
caption.zh: 【待译】11 December 1950: a court ruling on the custody of Maria Hertogh sets off three days of rioting; 18 people are killed and 173 injured.

caption.en: 12 May 1955: a bus workers' strike at Hock Lee turns into a riot; four people die, among them a police officer, a student and a journalist.
caption.zh: 【待译】12 May 1955: a bus workers' strike at Hock Lee turns into a riot; four people die, among them a police officer, a student and a journalist.

caption.en: October 1956: the government closes two Chinese school unions and students occupy their schools; when police clear them, rioting spreads and 13 people are killed.
caption.zh: 【待译】October 1956: the government closes two Chinese school unions and students occupy their schools; when police clear them, rioting spreads and 13 people are killed.

caption.en: 31 August 1957: the Federation of Malaya becomes independent, with Tunku Abdul Rahman as Prime Minister; Singapore remains a British colony.
caption.zh: 【待译】31 August 1957: the Federation of Malaya becomes independent, with Tunku Abdul Rahman as Prime Minister; Singapore remains a British colony.

caption.en: 30 May 1959: in the first fully elected Legislative Assembly, the People's Action Party wins 43 of the 51 seats.
caption.zh: 【待译】30 May 1959: in the first fully elected Legislative Assembly, the People's Action Party wins 43 of the 51 seats.

caption.en: 3 June 1959: Singapore becomes a self-governing state; on 5 June Lee Kuan Yew and his eight ministers are sworn in at City Hall.
caption.zh: 【待译】3 June 1959: Singapore becomes a self-governing state; on 5 June Lee Kuan Yew and his eight ministers are sworn in at City Hall.

caption.en: 27 May 1961: in Singapore, Tunku Abdul Rahman proposes bringing Malaya, Singapore, Sarawak, North Borneo and Brunei together.
caption.zh: 【待译】27 May 1961: in Singapore, Tunku Abdul Rahman proposes bringing Malaya, Singapore, Sarawak, North Borneo and Brunei together.

caption.en: 1 September 1962: Singapore votes in a referendum on the terms of merger; about 71 percent choose the government's option, and about a quarter cast blank votes.
caption.zh: 【待译】1 September 1962: Singapore votes in a referendum on the terms of merger; about 71 percent choose the government's option, and about a quarter cast blank votes.

caption.en: 2 February 1963: in Operation Coldstore, more than a hundred opposition politicians, unionists and students are detained without trial as alleged communist supporters.
caption.zh: 【待译】2 February 1963: in Operation Coldstore, more than a hundred opposition politicians, unionists and students are detained without trial as alleged communist supporters.

caption.en: 16 September 1963: Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak form Malaysia; Brunei stays out, and Indonesia launches its Confrontation.
caption.zh: 【待译】16 September 1963: Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak form Malaysia; Brunei stays out, and Indonesia launches its Confrontation.

caption.en: 21 July 1964: during a procession for the Prophet Muhammad's birthday, clashes between Malays and Chinese break out; by early August 23 people have died and 454 are injured.
caption.zh: 【待译】21 July 1964: during a procession for the Prophet Muhammad's birthday, clashes between Malays and Chinese break out; by early August 23 people have died and 454 are injured.

caption.en: September 1964: a second wave of riots begins in Geylang Serai; 13 people are killed and 106 injured, and curfews return.
caption.zh: 【待译】September 1964: a second wave of riots begins in Geylang Serai; 13 people are killed and 106 injured, and curfews return.

caption.en: 10 March 1965: Indonesian saboteurs bomb MacDonald House on Orchard Road; three people are killed.
caption.zh: 【待译】10 March 1965: Indonesian saboteurs bomb MacDonald House on Orchard Road; three people are killed.

caption.en: 9 August 1965: Malaysia's Parliament votes to let Singapore go, and Singapore becomes an independent country.
caption.zh: 【待译】9 August 1965: Malaysia's Parliament votes to let Singapore go, and Singapore becomes an independent country.

caption.en: 22 December 1965: Yusof Ishak becomes the first President of the Republic of Singapore.
caption.zh: 【待译】22 December 1965: Yusof Ishak becomes the first President of the Republic of Singapore.
